critiques.issue: Wrong evidence. H2.2 says leftover time comes from optimizer, update and launch overhead (fused optimizer, fully compiled step, SiLU). E010 swapped the adaptive_max_pool2d atomic backward for max_pool2d. That change matches none of H2.2's three items. E005 and the E003 profile already refuted H2.2's core premise: the step is GPU-bound and SGD is about 2% of it. Logging E010 as support for H2.2 makes a refuted mechanism look alive.
critiques.suggestion: Remove E010+ from H2.2 and mark H2.2 refuted or low-confidence (E005-). Open a new Lvl2 under H2 that matches the profile: 'non-conv kernels that are a visible share of GPU time (atomic/scatter backward, memory-bound BN/GELU elementwise ~18%) can be cut without changing the math'. Attach E010+ there.

critiques.target: Hypothesis statuses and confidences (H1.3.1, H2.2.1, H2.1, H3, H1.1.1)
critiques.issue: Every node is still 'open' and no confidence has moved. That holds after clean refutations (H1.3.1 E004-, H2.2.1 E005-), a clean support (H1.1.1 E001+), and a notebook finding that contradicts a Lvl1 outright: prepare is 0.06-0.15 s and non-step overhead is about 2%, while H3 claims more than 10%. H3 still sits at 0.50 and H2.2.1 at 0.40, so the tree no longer reflects what the loop has learned.
critiques.suggestion: Close H1.1.1 as supported and H1.3.1 and H2.2.1 as refuted. Mark H3 refuted, since the E001 timing and E003 profile show fixed overhead is about 2% of the run, not more than 10%, and drop H3.1 and H3.2 to maintenance status. Lower H1.3 to about 0.2 and H2 from 0.6 to about 0.3, because systems work has delivered about 3% in total against a claim of 10-30%.

critiques.issue: Evidence doesn't match the claim. H2.1 says compile plus channels_last plus half precision raises throughput a lot. E007 tested something else: cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune on a base that already had compile, channels_last and bf16 since E001. The H2.1 claim itself, and H2.1.1 (at least 20% faster than eager fp32), have never been tested because no eager baseline exists. Calling E007 a refutation of H2.1 is a category error.
critiques.suggestion: Either reattach E007 to a Lvl3 like 'max-autotune/cudnn.benchmark beats default compile by >=2%' (refuted), or leave H2.1 inconclusive. If H2.1.1 matters for the narrative, run the tip once in eager fp32/TF32 to measure it. Otherwise close it as 'untested, superseded'.

critiques.issue: This keep rests on one run inside the measured jitter. E003, an identical commit, drifted +0.9%. E008 drifted +0.9% in the direction its change predicted it should not. The notebook itself says differences under about 1.5% can't be told apart. E007 also cost 0.18 pp of accuracy, a re-draw that left only 0.12 pp of margin. And E008 reused cached Inductor autotune results, so autotune cache state is an uncontrolled variable between experiments.
critiques.suggestion: Clear the Inductor cache and rerun E010's commit and an E010 variant without the E007 settings 2-3 times each, interleaved. Keep max-autotune only if the paired mean gap is above about 1.5%. Report the build cache state with every timing result. The official PCIe A100 will autotune from a cold cache and may pick different kernels.

critiques.issue: The verdict reports only half the prediction. H1.1.2 says getting back to 0.753 needs at least 1 extra epoch beyond 8.5. E002 and E004 clear 0.753 at 9 epochs, only 0.5 more. That second clause is refuted. The TTA ≈ 0.65 pp ≈ 1.2 epochs reasoning can't be tested here and adds nothing.
critiques.suggestion: Split the verdict: 8.5 epochs below 0.753 is supported, and 'at least 1 extra epoch needed' is refuted (E002, E004). Better, rewrite H1.1.2 as a knee statement: 'knee lies in (8.5, 9] epochs for the current recipe'.

critiques.target: H1.1.3 and the 'curve steepens below 9 epochs' claim (E006 notebook)
critiques.issue: The '~1 pp/epoch below 9' slope compares E006 (built on E002, LS 0.3) with E004 (LS 0.2, 0.7560). Against its real parent E002 (0.7552), the drop is 0.42 pp per half-epoch. Each point is one 3-seed draw. Re-draw noise on the 3-seed mean is about 0.07-0.1 pp: E002/E004/E005/E007/E010 are essentially the same recipe and span 0.7542-0.7560. The 8.5-epoch run is also structurally different: half-permutation epoch and a compressed (t/T)^3 lookahead schedule. 'Concave curve, epoch trimming not viable' is a strong conclusion from three noisy points with mixed LS. H1.1.3 also predicted roughly linear behaviour, which the three points contradict, yet it is still marked inconclusive.
critiques.suggestion: Refute the linearity clause of H1.1.3 or rewrite it. Recompute slopes against the correct parent. Before ruling out epoch trimming, test 8.75 epochs on the tip, since a 0.25-epoch step is about 0.22 s (2.7%). Treat 'steepening' as tentative.

critiques.issue: The refutation of '≥0.3 pp gain from LS 0.3' holds. But the keep decision is a coin flip: +0.07 pp, with per-seed changes of -0.02, -0.16 and +0.40. The LS axis was probed at only two points. LS 0.1 and 0.4 were never run, so 'LS is not a strong lever' covers only the range 0.2-0.3.
critiques.suggestion: Record LS 0.2 as 'equivalent, kept by convention', not as a gain. If you revisit LS, do it together with the lookahead or EMA changes below; heavy averaging may change the optimal smoothing. A single LS 0.1 run is cheap if a sweep slot opens.

critiques.target: Surprising result: E008 (lookahead worth ~1 pp, ~3x predicted)
critiques.issue: This is the biggest accuracy effect in the log, and it went in the opposite direction from the CIFAR-10 intuition. None of H1-H4 explains it. A plausible reason is that end-of-training optimization noise dominates at 9 epochs on CIFAR-100: lr 9 with LS and 100 classes leaves the final iterates noisy, so averaging recovers a lot. If that is right, the lr tail, decay-to-zero shape, wd, and the averaging schedule (0.95^5·(t/T)^3, every 5 steps, inherited from CIFAR-10) are all untuned levers likely worth fractions of an epoch. Also, H4.2.1's 'raises per-seed std' clause was never checked. Per-seed ranges are 0.51 pp (E008) and 0.47 pp (E007), so no variance effect shows.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl2 under H1: 'final-iterate noise limits accuracy at <=9 epochs; averaging and annealing the tail are the strongest levers'. Falsifiable children: (a) a stronger or longer lookahead (higher base decay, k=3 vs 5) or an EMA over the last ~30% of steps gives ≥0.2 pp at 9 epochs; (b) a faster lr decay over the last epoch gives ≥0.2 pp; (c) a combined gain lets 8.5 epochs clear 0.753. Mark the std clause of H4.2.1 unsupported.

critiques.target: Untried directions: H1.2 (Muon), H1.4 (data selection), H1.5 (width), H2.3 (progressive resizing), lr/wd/batch size
critiques.issue: After 10 experiments the tip is the E001 recipe at 9 epochs plus two small systems tweaks. The 9.28 → 8.09 s gain is about 10% from dropping one epoch and about 3% from systems work. No experiment has tried to improve sample efficiency, which H1 calls the main driver. All recipe-changing runs so far were neutral or harmful ablations (LS, lookahead removal, fewer epochs). lr 9 and wd 0.012 come straight from CIFAR-10 and were never tuned for CIFAR-100. Width 512 vs 576 (H1.5.1) was never run.
critiques.suggestion: Shift the budget to positive-direction recipe experiments, ranked by expected payoff: lookahead/EMA and tail tuning (see above), a small lr/wd sweep at 9 epochs, Muon on conv filters (H1.2.1), then width. Deprioritize H1.4 and H2.3. At about 0.9 s/epoch and convs at 75% of GPU time, they need a large accuracy-per-FLOP win to pay off.

critiques.issue: H1's quantitative claim, 'from 59.3 s to roughly 10 s', was beaten by E001 (9.28 s), so it no longer guides anything. H1 also bundles five unrelated levers. The data now says averaging is huge, LS is flat, and epochs below 9 are steep. That distinction is lost in one blanket claim.
critiques.suggestion: Restate H1 with a new falsifiable target, e.g. 'recipe changes can move the knee below 8 epochs (≤7.3 s)'. Let the Lvl2 nodes carry the specific levers, ranked by observed effect size.

critiques.target: H2 remaining headroom (convs at ~30% of bf16 peak)
critiques.issue: The notebook concludes 'remaining systems levers are FLOP reductions, not kernel selection'. That rests on max-autotune winning only about 1%. But convs reaching about 95 TFLOP/s (30% of peak) is unexplained. The cause could be the small spatial sizes in late blocks, odd shapes from the 2x2 whitening (31x31 outputs?), or memory-bound BN/GELU around each conv. None of these is a hypothesis yet. The 18% elementwise share is also directly addressable: try GELU → ReLU/SiLU (cheaper and fusable), or fold BN into convs where possible.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl3 under the new non-conv-kernel node: 'GELU→ReLU (or SiLU) cuts step time ≥3% with accuracy within re-draw noise (±0.15 pp)'. Separately, profile per-layer conv TFLOP/s to see whether one layer shape drags the average down. A pad or crop that makes the whitening output 32x32 or 30x30 might help.

critiques.issue: E003 shows bit-identical reruns, but that only measures nondeterminism within one commit. E005 shows a change with identical math but a different compiled graph moved the mean by 0.18 pp. So any code change, systems changes included, re-draws accuracy with a 3-seed-mean sd of about 0.08-0.1 pp. Five near-identical recipes span 0.7542-0.7560. 'Supports' overstates how much protection H4.1.1 gives, and every systems keep carries accuracy risk at the current 0.21 pp margin.
critiques.suggestion: Re-scope H4.1.1 to 'bit-identical commit'. Add an explicit noise model to the tree: 3-seed-mean re-draw sd ≈ 0.09 pp, from E002/E004/E005/E007/E010. Mark accuracy deltas under about 0.25 pp '~' by rule, and verdict H4.1 as partially refuted, since compile-graph changes are not 'small' relative to the effects you test.

critiques.target: Constraint framing (0.753 local gate vs 40-seed official 0.75)
critiques.issue: The tip's 3-seed mean is 0.7551. With per-seed sd around 0.2-0.25 pp, the expected 40-seed mean is about 0.755 ± 0.13, well clear of 0.75. So the binding constraint is the local 0.753 gate on fixed seeds 0-2, not the official bar. That gate is a noisy judge, so repeatedly keeping changes that clear it invites winner's-curse selection on lucky re-draws. Seed 1 is consistently the weakest.
critiques.suggestion: For any candidate tip within 0.15 pp of 0.753, confirm on a few extra seeds offline (drafts/, not the scored run) before relying on it. Log per-seed results for every run so seed-specific weakness, like seed 1's, stays visible.

critiques.issue: All time conclusions come from an SXM4 card at 400 W. The official judge is a PCIe card at 300 W with lower sustained clocks and memory bandwidth. Autotune choices made under max-autotune and cudnn.benchmark may differ on PCIe, and cudnn.benchmark can choose different algorithms per run, which feeds the accuracy re-draw. No hypothesis covers whether the systems gains transfer.
critiques.suggestion: Add a note or Lvl3 under H2: 'systems gains measured on SXM keep their sign on PCIe'. At minimum, prefer changes that cut work (E010-style) over changes that depend on kernel selection (E007-style) when the gains are similar.

structured_output.summary:
The tree has fallen behind the results. Every node is still 'open' with its original confidence, even after clear refutations of H1.3.1, H2.2.1 and H3 (the notebook measured about 2% overhead, while H3 claims more than 10%). Several verdicts are attached to the wrong node. E010 (pool-backward swap) supports H2.2, whose launch-overhead premise E005 had already refuted. E007 (autotune and cudnn.benchmark) refutes H2.1, but H2.1 is about compile, channels_last and bf16, which the base already had. Two verdicts report only half their prediction: H1.1.2 and H4.2.1.

Several conclusions rest on single runs inside the noise. E007's -1.1% keep sits within the ±1% jitter the notebook measured itself. The '~1 pp/epoch below 9 epochs' steepening compares E006 against a parent with a different LS setting. LS 0.2 vs 0.3 is +0.07 pp against a re-draw sd of about 0.09 pp for the 3-seed mean; that estimate comes from five near-identical recipes spanning 0.7542-0.7560, and E005 shows even identical math re-draws accuracy.

Net progress is almost all one epoch cut plus about 3% of systems work. No experiment has improved sample efficiency, which H1 says is the main lever. The surprising result is E008: lookahead is worth about 1 pp, three times the prediction. No Lvl1 explains it. It points to end-of-training iterate noise as a major driver, which makes the untuned averaging schedule, the lr tail and lr/wd (all inherited from CIFAR-10) the most promising untried directions. Muon, width and GELU→ReLU should come before data selection and progressive resizing. Finally, the binding constraint is the noisy local 0.753 gate on fixed seeds, not the official 40-seed 0.75 bar. That creates winner's-curse risk on future keeps, and the SXM vs PCIe difference in judging hardware is untested for kernel-selection gains.
